four) is 03:30 and "pusastoņi" is 07:30 -- hence bare_half_to +
toward_hour_12h.  Latvian writes the prefix fused onto the hour cardinal, so
chronologia/extract/numfold_latvian.py splits the word and this file binds the
prefix it leaves behind.  Source: pronuncia.io, "How to Tell Time and Dates in

marker_half: "puse" (half) as the period noun of "first/second half of <year>".
marker_last: "pagājušajā" (last, past) as the backward determiner: the locative
definite form of the phrase Unicode CLDR 47 dateFields, locale lv, gives for
relative-type--1 ("pagājušajā nedēļā", "pagājušajā gadā").  Only that form
ships -- the participle has no dictionary declension table to transcribe, and
the remaining cells would be guesses.

unit_century: Declension: en.wiktionary.org.  A counted noun surfaces in more than one
form here.  After "pirms"/"pēc" it is the genitive singular when the numeral
ends in 1 (and is not 11) and the dative plural otherwise ("pirms gada",
"pirms 11 gadiem").  A bare count admits two registers -- formal genitive
plural after 11-19 and the round tens, colloquial nominative -- and both ship,
because nothing in the input says which register the writer used.
